basic.title: Basic Worksheet
basic.description: Fundamental concepts of Sets for building a strong base.

questions.text: Define a Set and give two examples.
Write the set A = {x : x is an integer and -3 < x < 7} in roster form.
Write the set B = {2, 4, 8, 16, 32} in set-builder form.
List all the elements of the set C = {x : x is an odd natural number}.
State whether the set of prime numbers is finite or infinite.
If A = {1, 2} and B = {1, 2, 3}, is A a subset of B?
Write all the subsets of the set A = {a, b}.
What is the power set of A = {1}?
For the sets in Q9, find A ∩ B.

standard.title: Standard Worksheet
standard.description: Standard board-level questions for exam preparation.

questions.text: If A and B are two sets such that n(A) = 17, n(B) = 23 and n(A ∪ B) = 38, find n(A ∩ B).
Draw a Venn diagram to represent (A ∪ B)'.
In a group of 400 people, 250 can speak Hindi and 200 can speak English. How many people can speak both Hindi and English?
If X and Y are two sets such that X has 40 elements, X ∪ Y has 60 elements and X ∩ Y has 10 elements, how many elements does Y have?
Show that A ∩ B = A ∩ C need not imply B = C.
Let A, B, and C be the sets such that A ∪ B = A ∪ C and A ∩ B = A ∩ C. Show that B = C.
Using properties of sets, show that A ∪ (A ∩ B) = A.
Find the union of each of the following pairs of sets: (i) X = {1, 3, 5} Y = {1, 2, 3} (ii) A = {a, e, i, o, u} B = {a, b, c}

hots.title: HOTS Worksheet
hots.description: High Order Thinking Skills questions for competitive exams (JEE Main).

questions.text: Two finite sets have m and n elements. The total number of subsets of the first set is 56 more than the total number of subsets of the second set. Find the values of m and n.

In a survey of 60 people, it was found that 25 people read newspaper H, 26 read newspaper T, 26 read newspaper I, 9 read both H and I, 11 read both H and T, 8 read both T and I, and 3 read all three newspapers. Find the number of people who read at least one of the newspapers.

In a town of 10,000 families it was found that 40% family buy newspaper A, 20% buy newspaper B and 10% buy newspaper C. 5% families buy A and B, 3% buy B and C and 4% buy A and C. If 2% families buy all the three newspapers, find the number of families which buy the newspaper A only.
Let A and B be sets. If A ∩ X = B ∩ X = ∅ and A ∪ X = B ∪ X for some set X, show that A = B.
Two sets A and B are such that n(A ∪ B) = 21, n(A' ∩ B') = 9, n(A ∩ B) = 7. Find n(A ∩ B'). (Assume Universal set U has 50 elements if not specified, or checks logic).
Let f: R → R be defined by f(x) = x² + 1. Find f⁻¹(17) and f⁻¹(-3).
If A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, define a relation R on A by R = {(x, y) : |x - y| is even}. Show that R is an equivalence relation.
Find the domain and range of the relation R defined by R = {(x, x + 5) : x ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}}.
Let A = {1, 2, 3, ..., 14}. Define a relation R from A to A by R = {(x, y) : 3x - y = 0, where x, y ∈ A}. Write down its domain, codomain and range.
Let A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}. Let R be the relation on A defined by {(a, b) : a, b ∈ A, b is exactly divisible by a}. Write R in roster form.
